findings.problem: One unmarked instance of the WEB-001 pattern remains after the repair, in a paragraph WEB-001 did not list (guidance/editorial.md, 'A text does what texts do': texts credited with the study's own inferences). L150-152: 'Between the two lessons the Alleluia asks, salutáre tuum da nobis, "grant us thy salvation": the salvation Paul has just called nearer is asked for as God's gift.' The Alleluia asks for 'thy salvation'. That this is the salvation Paul calls nearer in Rom 13:11 is the study's link, drawn through Aquinas's Advent sense (Super Rom. 13 lect. 3, 'nostra salus scilicet Christus') and Augustine's 'salutare tuum, Christum tuum' (En. in Ps. 84.9). The sentence states it as what the Alleluia asks, unmarked. The next sentence marks its own extension ('If Paul's words bear that sense'). A lesser instance is at L160-161, 'The Secret asks God for a cleansing like it'. The likeness to Paul's casting off is the study's comparison, and it is placed inside the Secret's request. The five sentences WEB-001 listed are repaired, and no other unmarked instance was found in the four interpretations, so this is an isolated instance.
findings.required_result: State each link in the study's own voice where it is drawn, without the colon that turns it into the Alleluia's content and without another 'If ...' formula. For example, at L150-152: 'Between the two lessons the Alleluia asks, salutáre tuum da nobis, "grant us thy salvation." Sung after the Epistle, the request can be taken as asking God to give the salvation Paul has just called nearer.' At L160-163: 'Paul makes the casting off of the works of darkness the hearers' own task. The Secret also asks for cleansing, but asks it of the holy gifts: that poténti virtúte, "by their mighty power," they make us mundátos and purióres, cleansed and purer.'

findings.problem: 'The night far spent becomes, in Chrysostom's hands, a household before dawn.' In Homilies on Romans 24, on v. 12 (registered CCEL passage, lines 46774-46778, artifact 8bdb50c6), the people are neighbours: 'we each of us awake our neighbor, although it be night still ... we hasten one another'. The quotation that follows at once contradicts the frame sentence. The three-document profile retells the scene as 'neighbors stirring and dressing before dawn' and asks a reviewer to check what an illustration's characters do. HOM-003 found the same word in the homily and named this line for the study's owner if the study was re-entered. It was re-entered at iteration 4, and the line is unchanged. Isolated.
findings.required_result: Retell the scene as Chrysostom gives it, for example: 'Chrysostom describes neighbours waking one another as the night ends.' Keep the quotation that follows.

findings.required_result: When research is next re-entered, record Sicard's Erunt signa paragraph in research/scope.md: the Epistle fitted to Prope est regnum Dei by Propior est nostra salus; benignitas as affectus bonus, the earth as caro and the fruit as opera bona; and the orations fitted to the second coming. summary: Cold study review 4 of the Claude 1962 First Sunday of Advent expansive study (main.tex; appointed_text_completeness = complete, Full PDF; all 22 sealed REVIEW_INPUTS files hash-matched). Read the opening and the four interpretations that moved, each repaired sentence against its earlier form (git diff to HEAD 7d290f7814): the five WEB-001 sentences (20 L85-88, L92-95; 30 L237-241; 40 L131-135; 50 L170-172) now mark the study's own link once, in varied ordinary words, and every clause that a source states is still attributed to that source, with no inference moved into a Father's mouth and no qualification dropped. Checked at the loci: Chrysostom Hom. in Rom. 24 on vv. 11 and 12 (registered CCEL passages, lines 46732-46768 and 46770-46804); Gregory Hom. in Ev. I.1.3 (tracked Wikisource artifact: 'festinare ad ea quantocius debemus', 'Qui ergo appropinquante mundi fine non gaudet, amicum se illius esse testatur'); Ambrose Exp. Luc. X.37 ('cum lumini coelesti vitia carnis obsistunt'); Bellarmine Ps 24 expl. 2-3 ('the certain hope of assistance'); Aquinas Super Ps. 24 n. 1, cps21.html refetched with SHA-256 5e8fdbbe matched ('in te Deus meus confido. 2 Cor. 3: fiduciam talem habemus per Christum ad Deum, non quod sufficientes simus'), which supports 40 L133-135. WEB-002's named link (label sec:date-location exists; \hyperref is a supported converter command), WEB-003's 'confído' and WEB-004's 'coelum igitur et terra et transibit et erit' (bound Bede artifact) are correct. Consequential-difficulty test: what salvation is 'nearer' and in what way. Aquinas, Super Rom. 13 lect. 3 (cro12.html refetched, SHA-256 1c3db878 matched) gives the Apostle's two senses (time; disposition by charity), then 'secundum quod Ecclesia haec verba adventus tempore legit ... ex persona omnium fidelium', 'quod tempus repraesentat Ecclesia ... nunc propior est nostra salus scilicet Christus', and 'tempus misericordiae'. The study teaches the question and his inference accurately at 40 L56-79 and L152-158 and 50 L78-90, and marks its own extensions ('If Paul's words bear that sense'; 'If in Advent the Church takes the place, as Aquinas says'). Second test: Augustine, En. in Ps. 84.9 (tracked Latin: 'Dedit enim nobis Christum, sed hominem: quem nobis dedit hominem, eum ipsum nobis daturus est Deum ... Deum enim Christum nullus hominum capere poterat'). 50 L9-39 poses why the Church still asks for Christ already given and gives Augustine's answer plainly and correctly. check-content-preflight (research edition, every check) passes and the document-type assembly is current. Limits: no print export was requested, so no page count. The concise study, homily and generated date appendix are outside this stage and were not reviewed as prose. Unchanged files (05, 10, 60, 90) were read for context only. Verdict: PASS, with no blocking finding. There are three new advisories: a remaining unmarked link at 40 L150-152 (with a lesser one at L161); Chrysostom's neighbours retold as 'a household' at 40 L31; and the iteration-4 production record's statement that the concise carries none of the WEB-001 sentences, when concise 10-commentary L222-225 and L323-327 carry instances 1 and 4. The standing advisories STU-017, STU-019 and STU-021 are unchanged and re-recorded.
